summary.text: A 69-year-old Japanese woman with DRPLA noticed gait disturbance and dysarthria at 61 years old, later developed visual disturbances and needed a cane. Her mother had gait disturbances in her 80s and a cousin had a psychotic disorder. She had right-eye cataract surgery with lens implantation at 67 years old.

Neurological examination showed reduced visual acuity, dysarthria, ataxic gait, coordination disturbances and pyramidal tract signs without dementia or myoclonus. MRI showed cerebellar and brainstem atrophy with periventricular white matter high-intensity signals. Genetic analysis showed an expanded allele with 55 CAG repeats and a normal allele with 15 repeats.

At ophthalmic examination, visual acuity was 20/200 in the right eye and 20/20 in the left. Slit lamp showed left-eye corneal swelling and guttata. Specular microscopy showed severely reduced endothelial cell density (483 and 444 cells/mm2) and reduced hexagonality, and OCT showed RNFL thinning corresponding to optic nerve atrophy.
